findings.body:
**Contain listener exceptions during normal output delivery.**

If a stdout or stderr listener throws on a newline-terminated line, `src/shared/proc.ts:431` lets the exception escape the stream's `data` callback. This can terminate the host instead of producing a managed result. Node invokes event listeners synchronously; exceptions from asynchronous callbacks require containment at the callback boundary. ([nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.16.0/docs/api/events.html?utm_source=openai))

The catch at Lines 540–544 protects only final unterminated lines. Isolate each listener invocation during normal delivery as well. Ensure that one listener failure does not skip other listeners or tail retention.
findings.title: Contain listener exceptions during normal output delivery.

findings.body:
**Do not treat leader closure as process-group termination.**

On POSIX, a descendant can ignore SIGTERM and redirect its stdio. If the leader exits, `child.close` resolves although the descendant remains alive. Node's `close` event covers the child and its stdio, not process-group termination. ([nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v22.16.0/docs/api/child_process.html))

At `src/shared/proc.ts:695–696`, this skips SIGKILL. During ordinary cancellation, Line 531 also removes the group from `activeChildren`, so later cleanup cannot reach it.

Track process-group termination separately from leader closure. Preserve the group identity and escalate surviving group members after the TERM grace.
findings.title: Do not treat leader closure as process-group termination.

findings.body:
**Use one `staleMs` value for each `lockPath`.**

`src/shared/gitMutex.ts:197` passes the caller's `staleMs` to proper-lockfile unchanged. Each caller checks the artifact age against its own `stale` value. By default, the holder refreshes the artifact every `stale / 2` ms, which is 15000 ms for the 30000 ms default. A caller with `staleMs: 2000` can therefore treat a live holder's artifact as stale at about 3000 ms and acquire the lock. The first holder's callback can then run at the same time as the new callback. The compromise is recorded only at the holder's next refresh, so both callbacks can start Git mutations before the wrapper reports it.

Require the same `staleMs` for every caller of a given `lockPath`. The sweep registry binds one mutex to its linked operations. `worktreeFor` and `cleanup` accept their own `mutex.staleMs` and `mutex.lockPath` inputs, and copy them into the mutex config. Reject a `staleMs` that differs from the registry-bound value for the same `lockPath`, or document the shared-value requirement at the input boundary.
findings.title: Use one `staleMs` value for each `lockPath`.
